title: Brandl et al. 2020 — Motor Imagery Under Distraction: An Open Access BCI Dataset
description: An open-access electroencephalography dataset of motor imagery brain-computer interface performance under six different distraction conditions. Sixteen healthy participants performed left versus right hand motor imagery while experiencing flickering video, number search tasks, news listening, eyes closed state, vibro-tactile stimulation, or no distraction. The dataset comprises 504 trials per subject acquired at 1000 Hz with 63 EEG channels, including one calibration run without feedback and six feedback runs under distinct distraction conditions.
methods_description: EEG data were recorded from 16 healthy participants at 1000 Hz sampling rate using 63 channels with nose reference and two BrainAmp amplifiers (Brain Products). Participants completed seven runs of 72 trials each: one calibration run without feedback or distraction, followed by six feedback runs with auditory cues indicating left or right hand motor imagery under different distraction conditions. Trial duration was 4.5 seconds with 2.5 second inter-trial intervals. Online classification employed Common Spatial Pattern (CSP) with Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA). EEG montage followed the standard 10-05 system with Ag/AgCl wet sensors on an EasyCap Fast'n Easy Cap.
